title: Other New Orleans musicians on medicine shows; Earl Humphrey
summary: Barry asks why so few New Orleans players worked medicine shows; Joe says many unknown ones did, and the shows only needed an hour of playing.

story.theme_name: Medicine shows, minstrels, circuses and the black theater circuit
story.community_name: On the road with minstrel, carnival and tent shows

blocks.x: Let me ask you this. We've established that not many of these medicine shows went to New Orleans, because the people were more sophisticated and wouldn't put up with that old jive. But let me ask you this. There's very few New Orleans musicians that I've heard of working medicine shows. Why do you think they didn't work medicine shows? Because the medicine shows didn't come in there and let them leave with them, or because they weren't interested in them?
Well, probably a lot of those musicians that you never heard of had worked medicine shows. They come from someplace.
The only one that I know of that worked medicine shows and services besides you was Earl Humphrey
Did you ever run across Earl Humphrey?

Willie's brother. You know who he was. A trombone player. He told me a similar story. I forget the medicine show that he was with. But he left town with a medicine show, and never did come back until the Seventies, when he came back to New Orleans. So in other words, you'd play for one hour. Well, you wouldn't play, but I mean, you'd entertain, like with the whole thing.
Yeah, that's what made the medicine shows so good. You play for one hour and you're through.
